title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
why_read: This paper makes a concrete, measurable case for partial fine-tuning of physical-layer autoencoders, with real resource trade-off numbers that matter for edge radio deployments.
analysis: End-to-end autoencoder communications replace traditional radio blocks like modulation and coding with a jointly trained neural network pair. The core problem addressed is that a model trained on simple AWGN noise degrades badly when deployed over realistic Rayleigh fading channels with hardware impairments. The proposed fix is to freeze most of the network and fine-tune only a small, carefully selected subset of layers, reducing compute and energy cost during adaptation. The paper quantifies this with MAC counts, energy figures, and bit error rate curves, which makes the trade-offs concrete and actionable for practitioners building real radio systems.
